Subtitle: Flight and airport board
Short Description: Track a flight, read an airport board, and save the ones you fly.
Full Description:
AeroSwift is a live flight tracker built on open ADS-B data: it shows where an aircraft is right now, how high and how fast it is flying, and when it was observed taking off and landing, without an account.

WHAT IT DOES
• Search by flight number (UA1691), airline (Lufthansa) or route (SFO-JFK), or browse the live traffic around your home airport.
• Open a flight for its live position, altitude, ground speed, track and vertical rate, its operator and ICAO 24-bit address, and the departure and arrival times observed by the receiver network.
• Open any airport's board and read the arrivals and departures observed there over the last 2 to 24 hours.
• Save the flights you follow to a watchlist on the device and refresh them with one tap.

ABOUT THE DATA
All flight data is live ADS-B data from the OpenSky Network — the endpoints AeroSwift uses need no key and no sign-up. OpenSky observes where aircraft actually are. It does not publish airline schedules, gates, terminals, aircraft types or arrival estimates, so AeroSwift does not show them. When OpenSky does not report a field, the app says so instead of filling the gap. Anonymous OpenSky access covers roughly the last 24 hours.

NO ACCOUNT
There is no login, no profile, and nothing to subscribe to. Saved flights and your settings stay on the device.

Subtitle: Duplicate contacts & photos
Short Description: Find duplicate contacts and identical photos. Clear the app's own cache.
Full Description:
AGCleaner finds duplicates. It does not claim to do anything else.

DUPLICATE CONTACTS
AGCleaner reads your address book and groups the entries that describe the same person, matching on phone number, email address or name. Each group tells you which of the three it matched on, so you can judge it yourself. AGCleaner never edits, merges or deletes a contact — it asks for read access only, shows you what it found, and stops there.

IDENTICAL PHOTOS
AGCleaner compares photos by content, not by appearance. Two photos are listed together only when their files are byte-for-byte identical, confirmed by a SHA-256 digest of the actual bytes. There is no "98% similar" score anywhere in the app, because nothing in it computes one, and a merely similar photo is a different photo. One copy in every group is always kept. You choose what goes, your device asks you to confirm it, and the total you are shown afterwards is the size of exactly the files the system reported it removed.

APP CACHE
The Cache tab measures AGCleaner's own temporary directory and can empty it. The figure is a real byte count taken by walking that directory, and the amount freed is the difference measured after the delete. No other app is touched.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
AGCleaner cannot free system memory, cannot clear another app's data, and cannot report your device's total free storage. Apps on iOS and Android are not permitted to do those things, so AGCleaner does not show a gauge pretending otherwise.

WHAT LEAVES YOUR DEVICE
Your photos, contacts and files never do. Matching, hashing and deleting all happen on the device, and every photo shown in the results is one of your own files. There is no account, no sign-in and no purchase.
The app does send anonymous diagnostics to Google Firebase: crash reports, performance measurements and basic usage statistics, so that problems can be found and fixed. They carry no name, no contact detail and no photo or file content, and they are not used for advertising.

ADS
AGCleaner is free and shows ads from Google AdMob: a banner below the tab content and, occasionally, a full-screen ad between tabs. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure those ads. The app does not track you across other companies' apps or websites, and where the law requires consent (for example in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland) Google asks for it first; you can change that choice later from the Privacy choices button in the header.

The interface is available in twelve languages, switchable from the globe in the header.

Short Description: Suggested replies that sound like you. Runs on your device. No account, no ads.
Full Description:
AGrammarly suggests replies to the messages you get, and it does the whole job on your phone.

—— How it works ——

Paste or type the message you received. AGrammarly offers three replies to choose from, each labelled: one casual, one professional, one short. Tap one to put it in your reply, adjust it if you like, then tap Copy and paste it into your messaging app. Long-press a suggestion to copy it straight away.

Suggestions come from a pattern set that ships inside the app, combined with the phrasings and emoji you use most. There is no model call and no suggestions server: the matching runs on the device, so it works with no signal at all.

—— It learns how you write ——

The more replies you copy into your messages, the more your own phrasing shows up in what it offers. Your most-used emoji move to the front. All of that is stored on your device, and Settings can delete every bit of it in one action.

It is a practice surface inside this app — AGrammarly does not install a system keyboard, so it does not appear in your keyboard list for use in other apps.

—— What it keeps ——

No account. No sign-up. No ads and no analytics. Nothing you type leaves the phone: this build ships with no suggestions service configured. Your learned style and your counters live on the device and nowhere else.

The one thing the app can send is a crash report. If AGrammarly crashes, Google Firebase Crashlytics receives the technical details of the crash and an anonymous installation ID, so the bug can be fixed. It does not include your messages or anything the app has learned.

—— Honest about what it is not ——

AGrammarly is a reply helper, not a grammar or spelling checker, and not a writing assistant powered by a language model. It suggests replies; it does not correct your text. Suggestions and the keyboard are in English only.

Subtitle: Translate, talk & learn
Short Description: Translate typed or spoken phrases, practise speaking, and study phrases that stick.
Full Description:
Verba is a translator you can talk to, and a way to keep what you learn.

—— Translate ——

TRANSLATE
Type a phrase and get it back in the language you need, in 12 languages.

VOICE
Tap the mic, say a phrase, and Verba translates it when you finish speaking.

CONVERSATION
Two people take turns: each speaks in their own language and the other side shows the translation.

—— Learn ——

PRACTICE
Say real phrases for situations like the airport, a restaurant or a hotel, and see which words the speech recogniser heard.

FLASHCARDS
Spanish, French and Mandarin phrase decks with spaced repetition: each card comes back when it is due, and your review dates are kept on your phone.

PHRASEBOOK
Save any translation with one tap and find it again in your phrasebook.

—— Built to be used ——

• Text-to-speech, so you hear how it should sound
• Material 3 interface with glassmorphic cards
• Notification reminders for your streak and practice, using inexact alarms
• The microphone is optional: typing works without it
• No account needed to start

—— Ads ——

Verba is free and may show ads through Google AdMob. There are no in-app purchases and no paid tier.

—— About translation quality ——

Translation and speech recognition are automated and imperfect, especially with accents, background noise, idiom and specialist vocabulary. Do not rely on Verba for medical, legal, financial, safety or immigration matters — use a qualified human interpreter.

Subtitle: Play, record & compose
Short Description: Play 8 virtual instruments, arrange song sections, record mic takes.
Full Description:
VirtuBand is a music studio that fits in your pocket. Play eight synthesised instruments with your fingers, arrange a song in sections and play it back on a step sequencer, record takes with your microphone, and start from a genre drum pattern or a common chord progression when you cannot find the next part.

—— Play ——

Eight synthesised instruments — piano, guitar, bass, violin, drums, synth, flute and saxophone — each with its own playable surface rather than one generic keyboard: piano keys, a 12-fret fingerboard, eight drum pads, an XY pad for synth pitch and filter, and wind keys with a breath slider. Every sound is generated on your device, so it works offline.

—— Arrange ——

STUDIO
Pick which instruments play, set the tempo, and press Play: a 16-step sequencer plays them through your song sections in order, following each section's key.

TRACKS
Build the song structure by adding and removing sections such as verse, chorus, bridge and outro. The Studio plays them in order.

—— Record ——

RECORDINGS
Record a take with your microphone. Every take is saved on your device, where you can play it back, rename it, or delete it. Each take is a single microphone recording; VirtuBand does not overdub or mix takes together.

—— Compose ——

AI COMPOSE
Preview a starter drum pattern for pop, hip-hop, jazz or classical, then send it to the Studio as your drum part, and browse common chord progressions. These are built-in templates, not AI-generated.

JAM
Practise along with a metronome on the instrument of your choice, right on the same screen. Jam runs on your device only; there is no online multiplayer.

—— Built to get out of your way ——

• Dashboard summarising your recordings, sections and instruments
• Dark interface designed for playing in low light
• Sign-in is optional — tap "Continue as Guest" and every feature is available
• Works offline; nothing you record needs a network to save

Subtitle: Connection facts, measured
Short Description: Wi-Fi connection facts from your device, plus a real HTTPS speed test
Full Description:
WiFiTrail tells you what your device's connection actually is, and measures how fast it actually runs.

CONNECTION
The Connection tab reports the transport your device is using, straight from the operating system: Wi-Fi, cellular, ethernet, VPN, or several at once. On Wi-Fi it shows the network name and access point where the system releases them, and lists the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses this device holds on its own interfaces. Where the system withholds the network name, WiFiTrail says so, explains why, and offers the one step that can change it, instead of showing a placeholder. Refresh re-reads the OS, and the screen also updates itself when the connection changes.

SPEED TEST
The speed test transfers real bytes over HTTPS to and from Cloudflare's measurement endpoint. It reports download, upload, median ping and jitter, and prints the megabytes moved and the seconds taken underneath each figure so you can check the arithmetic. Before the first run every reading is a dash and the caption says it has not been measured. If a run is cancelled, times out, or fails, it ends with the reason in plain words and no number at all. When the device is offline, the test does not start and the screen says so.

SECURITY
Five pieces of general Wi-Fi guidance, labelled as advice rather than a scan. WiFiTrail gives your network no score and no pass or fail, because it cannot inspect your router, firewall, DNS or open ports.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
No app on iOS or Android is allowed to list the other networks around you, so WiFiTrail does not offer that, and it says so on screen rather than leaving an empty list. It reports no ISP, gateway, DNS or channel, because a sandboxed app cannot obtain them.

PERMISSIONS AND PRIVACY
Location is requested only when you tap Show network name on the Wi-Fi card, and for one reason: the system releases the Wi-Fi network's name to an app only once that permission is granted. WiFiTrail takes no location fix, stores no location and sends none. There is no account, no sign-in and no analytics. What leaves your device is the speed test's own traffic, crash reports, and ad requests to Google; the app puts no Wi-Fi name, local address or location into any of them. Deny location and everything else still works.

ADS
WiFiTrail is free and shows ads from Google AdMob: a banner below the tab content, and now and then a full-screen ad after you switch tabs. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure those ads. The ads are non-tracking: the app never asks to track you across other companies' apps. Where the law requires consent (the EEA, the UK and Switzerland), no ad is requested until you have made a choice, and a Privacy choices button in the header lets you change it. The banner is removed while a speed test runs.

LANGUAGES
The interface is translated into twelve languages: English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish. It follows your device language, and a picker in the app overrides it.
